intro: The Foresta Umbra is the state forest at the centre of the Gargano promontory, and its tree to see is the Faggio dei Baracconi, a beech 5.2 metres round and 26 metres tall, one of five Puglia trees in the ministry's national book of monumental trees. It stands at Baracconi, where one of the forest's fifteen marked trails begins. The forest is free and open, with parking at the trailheads.
meta_description: The Faggio dei Baracconi, a 5.2 m beech in the Foresta Umbra on the Gargano, in Italy's national book of monumental trees: where it stands, how to visit.
question_meta: The Faggio dei Baracconi is a monumental beech in the Foresta Umbra, at Baracconi where trail 3 begins on the road from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste.
question_answer: The tree to see in the Foresta Umbra is the Faggio dei Baracconi, a beech 5.2 metres round and 26 metres tall at Baracconi, where trail 3 begins on the road from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste. It was one of five Puglia trees chosen for Italy's national book of monumental trees. The forest is free and open.
question_context: The Foresta Umbra covers the high centre of the Gargano promontory in northern Puglia, a state forest of beech, oak and maple inside the Gargano National Park, and its old beech stands are part of the UNESCO World Heritage listing of Europe's ancient beech forests. Puglia's register of monumental trees lists four beeches in it, and the two thickest are 5.2 metres round. One of them, at Baracconi, is the beech that went into the ministry's national book Alberi monumentali d'Italia in 2019 as one of five trees from Puglia; the register gives it 26 metres tall. Nobody has published its age. The forest has fifteen marked trails with parking at the trailheads, and trail 3 starts at Baracconi on the road from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste. The register's group of old yews at Falascone stands in a fenced reserve kept for research, and only its fence line can be walked. There is no regular public transport into the forest; the road in runs from Vico del Gargano and Monte Sant'Angelo by way of Villaggio Umbra.

faq.q: Can you visit the old yews of the Foresta Umbra?
faq.a: Not up close. The register's yews at Falascone stand in a fenced reserve kept for research, and visitors can only walk along the fence. The Faggio dei Baracconi stands outside it, where trail 3 begins.

faq.q: How big is the Faggio dei Baracconi?
faq.a: Puglia's register of monumental trees gives it 5.2 metres round and 26 metres tall, level with the thickest beech it lists in the forest.

trees.story:
In 2019 this beech was one of five trees from Puglia chosen for the ministry's national book of monumental trees, Alberi monumentali d'Italia, standing in for the old beech woods of the Gargano. Puglia's register of monumental trees gives it 5.2 metres round and 26 metres tall, which puts it level with the Valle del Tesoro beech as the thickest beech the register lists anywhere in the Foresta Umbra.

The Foresta Umbra is the shaded centre of the Gargano promontory, a state forest of beech, oak and maple inside the Gargano National Park, and its old beech stands belong to the UNESCO World Heritage listing of Europe's ancient beech forests. This tree grows at Baracconi, on the road that crosses the forest from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste, where one of the forest's fifteen marked trails begins.

Nobody has published its age, and nothing dated records it in recent years, so if you have stood under it, tell us how it looked. The forest itself is free and open, with parking at the trailheads. The forest's famous old yews at Falascone are a different matter: they stand in a fenced reserve kept for research, and only the fence line can be walked.
trees.how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as a beech more than five metres round at Baracconi, where trail 3 begins on the road from Villaggio Umbra towards Vieste.
